cells.note: vllm bench serve (the torch side's own client and settings: in 1024, out 256, 16 requests, 2 warmups), scr serve --max-num-seqs 8 --max-model-len 8704, measured on nickm4 at this commit.
vllm bench serve (the torch side's own client and settings: in 1024, out 256, 16 requests, 2 warmups), scr serve --max-num-seqs 8 --max-model-len 8704, measured on nickm4 at this commit.

Measured at a 128-token prompt. The previous sweep's 132 ms was a 21-token prompt (`scr chat --bench`), which measures 116 ms on this commit. At 128 rows fp8 prefill runs within 3% of fp16 (158 vs 163 ms of device compute): the per-row activation quantize offsets the halved weight bytes.

moved.what: 32-core decode fill: each one-row projection streams on all 32 cores — measured in a same-binary A/B at 8b fp16, ITL −13.9 ms at ~123 (143.2 → 129.3), −13.9 at ~1k, −14.5 at ~10k. This sweep's 8b cells (131.2 / 138.7 / 179.7 ms) put short-context decode ahead of torch-spyre's 143.

512-row prompt chunks, each continuation on the narrowest prefix rung that finishes it: 8b ~10k TTFT −24.1% (17.29 → 13.13 s, byte-identical replies), 2b −3.3% at ~10k and −6.8% at ~2k; this sweep's 12.80 s and 8.15 s are both ahead of torch-spyre (13.04 / 8.23 s).
one persistent stream per session (resolved fences retire at completion; no per-token stream recreate) — RSS flat over 1,506 decode steps.
one --max-model-len law: a default granite `scr chat` loads again; an over-budget ask is refused with the number that fits.
whole-dxp matmuls past a measured 150 MiB per-core kernel slab take frontend trips, so gemma-4 31b bakes (it died at dxp's EAR overflow).

levers.work: 131 ms at ~123 against the card's ≈110 ms floor (16.4 GB/token at 149 GB/s) — the rest is attention and elementwise glue.
torch-spyre 1.10× ahead — the hd128 K/V gather kept in LX, projected −23 ms/step (≈156 ms).
torch-spyre 1.39× ahead — wide elementwise ops split by rows run at half rate; splitting their sticks is measured 2.05× faster on the op (PR in validation), and #622 extends it to column windows.
~10% of 2b fp8 short-context ITL is host time between steps — compile-time CB replay with the next token chosen on the device (#603).

at 128 prompt rows fp8 is no faster than fp16 — the per-token activation quantize chain grows with rows and eats the halved weight stream; fusing the quantize into the matmul (the device's fused per-token quantize) is the lever.

torch-spyre 1.57× ahead at 2b, 1.86× at 8b — batched decode TPOT 117 ms (2b) against torch-spyre's 82; the stick-axis elementwise split now in validation covers the batched rungs, and compile-time CB replay (#603) removes the per-step host gap.

conc: The previous sweep's conc-8 cells (77.2 / 28.9 tok/s) have no recoverable harness record. The last fully recorded run, 2026-10-13, measured 2b at 52.0 tok/s, TPOT p50 147.7 ms; this sweep measures 60.8 tok/s, TPOT p50 117.4 ms.
decode: Short-context parity is a shared floor: both stacks stream 16.4 GB of fp16 weights per token. Measured on the card (17 Oct), one fp16 matmul streams at most ~149 GB/s, and only across all 32 cores — the cost model's 204.8 GB/s peak is not reachable — so fp16 at one request bottoms out near 110 ms/token.

This sweep's harness differs from 2026-10-17's (64–128 output tokens, 1051/10086-token prompts, prefix caching not stated): prefix caching is now disabled, prompts are server-recorded at 128/1061/10091 tokens, and every cell takes 128 output tokens with ignore_eos. Cross-sweep deltas no PR accounts for — 2b fp16 ITL 45.6 → 42.2 ms at ~123 — are the harness, not code; TTFT cells compare the same way, prompt lengths differing sweep to sweep.
